timeout 15
silent_menu false
use_graphics_for linux
default_selection "pearOS NiceC0re"

# Ploader is rEFInd 0.14.1, so it follows rEFInd's two-level menu model: an
# auto-detected kernel produces ONE main-menu tile, and the extra lines of
# ploader_linux.conf become sub-entries you have to press Insert/F2 to reach.
#
# To get all three options on the main menu they have to be explicit
# `menuentry` stanzas here instead. `also_scan_dirs` is deliberately gone: it
# was what made Ploader auto-detect the kernel under /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/%ARCH%,
# and leaving it on would add a fourth, duplicate tile next to these three.
#
# `volume` is omitted on purpose -- rEFInd then resolves the paths on the volume
# it was launched from, which is efiboot.img in both the ESP and the El Torito
# case, and that is where _make_boot_on_fat puts the kernel.
#
# One `initrd` per stanza is a hard requirement, not a style choice: recent
# kernels dropped cmdline multi-initrd support, so build-binary concatenates the
# microcode images and the real initramfs into this single file.

menuentry "pearOS NiceC0re arch (x86_64, UEFI)" {
    icon    /EFI/BOOT/theme/icons/os_pearos.png
    loader  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/%ARCH%/vmlinuz-linux
    initrd  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/%ARCH%/initramfs-linux.img
    options "archisobasedir=%INSTALL_DIR% archisolabel=%ARCHISO_LABEL% cow_spacesize=4G module_blacklist=pcspkr i915.modeset=1 amdgpu.modeset=1 radeon.modeset=1 nvme_load=yes quiet splash"
}

menuentry "pearOS NiceC0re arch (x86_64, UEFI), No Plymouth (Debug)" {
    icon    /EFI/BOOT/theme/icons/os_linux.png
    loader  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/%ARCH%/vmlinuz-linux
    initrd  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/%ARCH%/initramfs-linux.img
    options "archisobasedir=%INSTALL_DIR% archisolabel=%ARCHISO_LABEL% cow_spacesize=4G module_blacklist=pcspkr i915.modeset=1 amdgpu.modeset=1 radeon.modeset=1 nvme_load=yes plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles"
}

menuentry "pearOS NiceC0re arch (x86_64, UEFI), Legacy Hardware (GPU nomodeset)" {
    icon    /EFI/BOOT/theme/icons/os_recovery.png
    loader  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/%ARCH%/vmlinuz-linux
    initrd  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/%ARCH%/initramfs-linux.img
    options "archisobasedir=%INSTALL_DIR% archisolabel=%ARCHISO_LABEL% cow_spacesize=4G module_blacklist=nvidia,nvidia_modeset,nvidia_uvm,nvidia_drm nomodeset nvme_load=yes"
}

# This file is NOT what draws the boot menu any more -- ploader.conf does, via
# explicit `menuentry` stanzas, so that all three options show up on the main
# screen instead of behind Insert/F2.
#
# It is kept for two reasons: build-binary's bootmode validation fails if it is
# missing, and it is the fallback if `also_scan_dirs` is ever put back into
# ploader.conf. Only the default entry lives here on purpose -- keeping all
# three duplicated in two files would just be two places to forget.
#
# GPU driver selection is not done from the boot menu at all: the
# nvidia-module-loader script (wired up by /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-loader.conf)
# asks chwd what the GPU is and loads nouveau or the open nvidia modules
# accordingly, which is what the old driver=free / driver=nonfree entries used
# to switch between.
#
# Never add `modprobe.blacklist=nouveau` here or in ploader.conf: on a
# pre-Turing GPU the open nvidia module refuses to load, and with nouveau
# blacklisted the machine would end up with no driver at all.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#This script runds inside airootfs chroot during build
# it's executed automatically by mkarchiso

set -e -u

# Function to ask for continuation on error
ask_continue() {
	local error_msg="$1"
	echo ""
	echo "ERROR: $error_msg"
	echo ""
	read -p "Do you want to continue? (y/N): " answer < /dev/tty
	if [[ ! "$answer" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
		echo "Aborting script execution..."
		exit 1
	fi
	echo "Continuing..."
}

echo "==========================="
echo "Customizing pearOS Live env"
echo "==========================="

echo "Setting OS release"
echo "pearOS" > /etc/arch-release && \
	echo "OS release updated" ||\
	echo "Failed to set OS release"

if command -v plymouth-set-default-theme &> /dev/null; then
	echo "Setting plymouth theme"
	plymouth-set-default-theme -R pear-plymouth && \
		echo "Success!" || \
		echo "Failed to set plymouth theme"
else
	echo "Plymouth command theme not found"
fi

echo "############################################################################################################################"
echo "###						REGENERATING PACMAN KEYS					       ###"
echo "############################################################################################################################"
# Ensure gnupg directory exists with correct permissions
mkdir -p /etc/pacman.d/gnupg
chmod 700 /etc/pacman.d/gnupg

# Temporarily disable exit on error for pacman-key operations
set +e

# Initialize pacman keyring if it doesn't exist
if [ ! -d /etc/pacman.d/gnupg/private-keys-v1.d ] || [ ! -f /etc/pacman.d/gnupg/pubring.gpg ]; then
	echo "Initializing pacman keyring..."
	pacman-key --init
	if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
		ask_continue "pacman-key --init failed"
	fi
fi

# Populate all installed keyrings (archlinux, pearos, ...)
echo "Populating GPG keyrings..."
pacman-key --populate
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
	ask_continue "pacman-key --populate failed"
fi

# Re-enable exit on error
set -e

echo "Installing pearOS plasma-welcome (replaces stock version via --overwrite)"
if pacman -S --noconfirm --overwrite='*' plasma-welcome; then
        mkdir -p /etc/skel/.config/autostart
        cp -r /usr/share/applications/welcome.desktop /etc/skel/.config/autostart/welcome.desktop ||:
        echo "plasma-welcome installed successfully"
else
        echo "Failed to install pearOS plasma-welcome"
fi


echo "Fixing permissions"
if chmod -R 0755 /usr/share/extras/; then
        echo "Permissions set!"
else
        echo "Failed to set permissions"
fi


echo "Installing CMake"
if pacman -S --noconfirm cmake extra-cmake-modules; then
        echo "CMake and Extra CMake Modules Installed!"
else
        echo "Failed to install CMake + Extra Modules"
fi

echo "Downloading Liquid Gel"
if git clone https://github.com/pearOS-archlinux/liquid-gel; then
        echo "Liquid Gel Downloaded..."
else
        echo "Failed to download Liquid Gel"
fi

echo "Compiling Liquid Gel"
if cd liquid-gel && mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr && make -j$(nproc) && sudo make install; then
        echo "Liquid Gel Compiled..."
else
        echo "Failed to Compile Liquid Gel - Build Failed"
fi



echo "Cleaning up pearOS Build"

rm -rf /usr/share/{doc,man,info,help}/*
pacman -Scc --noconfirm
if [ ! -L /sbin/init ]; then
    ln -sf /usr/lib/systemd/systemd /sbin/init
fi
echo "Cleanup"
if rm -rf /root/liquid-gel; then
        echo "Finish cleanup"
else
        echo "Failed to Cleanup files"
fi
echo "==================="
echo "Script run complete"
echo "==================="
sync

files.pear/airootfs/usr/local/bin/alg-finalisa:
#!/bin/bash

chmod 750 /etc/sudoers.d
chmod 750 /etc/polkit-1/rules.d
chgrp polkitd /etc/polkit-1/rules.d
chmod -v 750 /root

rm -vf /etc/sudoers.d/g_wheel
rm -vf /etc/sddm.conf.d/autologin.conf
rm -vf /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/49-nopasswd_global.rules
rm -vf /root/{.automated_script.sh,.zlogin}

# --- pacman keyring: hand the installed system a real, persistent one --------
#
# pacman-init.service and etc-pacman.d-gnupg.mount are live-session machinery:
# the mount puts /etc/pacman.d/gnupg on tmpfs and the service rebuilds the
# keyring into it at every boot. Both survive unpackfs into the installed
# system, where the effect is a keyring that lives in RAM and is thrown away on
# every reboot -- so `pacman-key --lsign-key` never persists, and every boot
# pays for a full --populate.
#
# Order matters here. The tmpfs is what currently masks the build host's
# keyring, which pacstrap copied into airootfs (Arch + Manjaro + our own keys,
# plus whatever local trust the build machine had). Removing the units without
# reinitialising would expose that copy as the installed system's keyring.
# So: drop the units, delete the inherited keyring, then build a fresh one from
# the keyring packages actually shipped (archlinux, cachyos, pearos).
rm -vf /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/pacman-init.service
rm -vf /etc/systemd/system/pacman-init.service
rm -vf /etc/systemd/system/etc-pacman.d-gnupg.mount
rm -rf /etc/pacman.d/gnupg
pacman-key --init
pacman-key --populate

sed -i 's/GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR=.*/GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR="pearOS NiceC0re"/' /etc/default/grub
sed -i 's/${GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR} Linux/${GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR}/' /etc/grub.d/10_linux

# Remove calamares-desktop from Desktop
rm -f /home/liveuser/Desktop/calamares.desktop

# Copy skel/.config in /root
cp -r /etc/skel/.config /root/

# The smart NVIDIA loader is a live-session mechanism only. On the installed
# system chwd has already put the correct driver branch in place, and the loader
# would override it: it decides from `chwd --list`, which reports the profiles
# *available* for the hardware, not the one installed. On a Pascal card that
# lists nvidia-dkms-580xx and would send the machine back to nouveau.
rm -vf /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-loader.conf
rm -vf /usr/local/bin/nvidia-module-loader

rm -f /usr/local/bin/{alg-finalisation,livecd-sound,Installation_guide}

# Enabling auto-login for 'default' user :
echo "[Autologin]" > /etc/sddm.conf
echo "User=default" >> /etc/sddm.conf
echo "Session=plasma.desktop" >> /etc/sddm.conf

pacman -R --noconfirm kinfocenter plasma-disks plasma-sdk
pacman -R --noconfirm gnome-software electron npm 

echo "Removing desktop entries..."
rm -rf /usr/share/applications/avahi-discover.desktop \
       /usr/share/applications/bssh.desktop \
       /usr/share/applications/bvnc.desktop \
       /usr/share/applications/qv4l2.desktop \
       /usr/share/applications/qvidcap.desktop \
       /usr/share/applications/org.kde.plasma.emojier \
       /usr/share/applications/calamares*

echo "Installing yay"
       git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/yay.git && cd yay && makepkg -si --noconfirm && rm -rf yay

sync

files.pear/airootfs/etc/mkinitcpio.conf:
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later

# vim:set ft=sh
# MODULES
# The following modules are loaded before any boot hooks are
# run.  Advanced users may wish to specify all system modules
# in this array.  For instance:
#     MODULES=(piix ide_disk reiserfs)
# nouveau is deliberately absent: nvidia-module-loader decides at runtime
# whether an NVIDIA GPU gets nouveau or the open nvidia modules. Loading nouveau
# from the initramfs would pre-empt that decision on every machine.
# i915/amdgpu stay -- they are listed explicitly, so they still load early and
# keep Plymouth on the native KMS driver for Intel/AMD.
MODULES=(i915 amdgpu vmwgfx virtio_gpu)

# BINARIES
# This setting includes any additional binaries a given user may
# wish into the CPIO image.  This is run last, so it may be used to
# override the actual binaries included by a given hook
# BINARIES are dependency parsed, so you may safely ignore libraries
BINARIES=()

# FILES
# This setting is similar to BINARIES above, however, files are added
# as-is and are not parsed in any way.  This is useful for config files.
FILES=()

# HOOKS
# This is the most important setting in this file.  The HOOKS control the
# modules and scripts added to the image, and what happens at boot time.
# Order is important, and it is recommended that you do not change the
# order in which HOOKS are added.  Run 'mkinitcpio -H <hook name>' for
# help on a given hook.
# 'base' is _required_ unless you know precisely what you are doing.
# 'udev' is _required_ in order to automatically load modules
# 'filesystems' is _required_ unless you specify your fs modules in MODULES
# Examples:
##   This setup specifies all modules in the MODULES setting above.
##   No raid, lvm2, or encrypted root is needed.
#    HOOKS=(base)
#
##   This setup will autodetect all modules for your system and should
##   work as a sane default
#    HOOKS=(base udev autodetect block filesystems)
#
##   This setup will generate a 'full' image which supports most systems.
##   No autodetection is done.
#    HOOKS=(base udev block filesystems)
#
##   This setup assembles a pata mdadm array with an encrypted root FS.
##   Note: See 'mkinitcpio -H mdadm' for more information on raid devices.
#    HOOKS=(base udev block mdadm encrypt filesystems)
#
##   This setup loads an lvm2 volume group on a usb device.
#    HOOKS=(base udev block lvm2 filesystems)
#
##   NOTE: If you have /usr on a separate partition, you MUST include the
#    usr, fsck and shutdown hooks.
#HOOKS=(base udev modconf memdisk archiso_shutdown archiso archiso_loop_mnt archiso_pxe_common archiso_pxe_nbd archiso_pxe_http archiso_pxe_nfs archiso_kms plymouth block filesystems keyboard)
# 'kms' removed: without autodetect it pulls in every DRM driver, nouveau
# included, which would defeat nvidia-module-loader.
HOOKS=(base udev modconf memdisk archiso archiso_loop_mnt archiso_pxe_common archiso_pxe_nbd archiso_pxe_http archiso_pxe_nfs plymouth block filesystems keyboard)

# COMPRESSION
# Use this to compress the initramfs image. By default, gzip compression
# is used. Use 'cat' to create an uncompressed image.
#COMPRESSION="gzip"
#COMPRESSION="bzip2"
#COMPRESSION="lzma"
#COMPRESSION="xz"
#COMPRESSION="lzop"
#COMPRESSION="lz4"
COMPRESSION="zstd"

# COMPRESSION_OPTIONS
# Additional options for the compressor
#COMPRESSION_OPTIONS=()

# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later

title   pearOS NiceC0re arch (x86_64, UEFI), No Plymouth (Debug)
linux   /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/x86_64/vmlinuz-linux
initrd  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/intel-ucode.img
initrd  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/amd-ucode.img
initrd  /%INSTALL_DIR%/boot/x86_64/initramfs-linux.img
options archisobasedir=%INSTALL_DIR% archisolabel=%ARCHISO_LABEL% cow_spacesize=4G module_blacklist=pcspkr i915.modeset=1 amdgpu.modeset=1 radeon.modeset=1 nvme_load=yes plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles
